subject: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)
body:
From: Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 10:12 AM
Subject: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

Hey Sean (cc Rafael) — we’re ready to wire up the first pass of cache hit-rate regression alerts alongside the v2 cache telemetry rollout.

Request: SRE sign-off on thresholds + paging policy + rollout sequence.

Proposal (high-level):
1) “Cache hit-rate regression” warning (non-paging):
- Signal: hit_rate (request-weighted), segmented by deployment_mode + region
- Condition: drop >= 7 percentage points vs trailing 7d baseline for >= 45 minutes
- Audience: #eng-sre-alerts (no pager)

2) “Cache hit-rate regression” page (paging):
- Same segmentation, but stricter + burn-rate style
- Condition: drop >= 12 percentage points vs 7d baseline for >= 30 minutes AND saved_prefill_ms down >= 25% vs baseline
- Audience: oncall-sre (pager)

Noise controls:
- Only evaluate segments with >= 2k req/30m
- Dampening: 2 hours between pages per segment
- Top-N segment limit (max 6 segments evaluated) to avoid explosion

Runbook: points to data quality checks + how to tell “real regression” vs traffic mix changes.

Rollout suggestion:
- Start in us-east-1 Hosted tier first (flagged), then Dedicated, then EU.
- Timing: align with ENG-4817 / observability-pack PR-921 landing early next week.

Attaching the current proposal PDF + preview screenshot from staging.

If you’re OK with the direction, I’ll convert the proposal into the final alert templates and tag Rafael for oncall impact review.

Thanks,
Sergio
—
Sergio Costa
SRE / Observability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 12:04 PM
Subject: Re: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

Thanks. A few questions before I sign off:

1) Baseline definition: trailing 7d baseline is per-segment (deployment_mode+region) computed hourly? Any guard against “baseline drift” when the new telemetry flags gradually enable?

2) I like the saved_prefill_ms coupling on the pager, but is that metric trustworthy under partial-prefill (i.e., we don’t want to page on accounting changes)?

3) The “Top-N segment limit” — what’s the ranking key (highest traffic?) and where is that enforced (query vs aggregator)?

4) Oncall impact: can we commit to (a) no pager for Dedicated until after 48h of Hosted stability and (b) a hard rollback switch (disable alert + telemetry flag) that Connor can run without engineering involved?

If we can address these, I’m good to proceed.

Sean

---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 12:37 PM
Subject: Re: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

+1 to Sean’s questions.

On oncall impact: I’m strongly in favor of “non-paging only” for the first 24–48h in a single region, because we already saw tag blowups in prior telemetry changes.

Also: can we add an explicit “tag explosion / cardinality guardrail triggered” alert (non-paging) that routes to the same runbook? That’s usually the early signal that makes everything else noisy.

Rafael

---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 1:28 PM
Subject: Re: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

Jumping in on (1) and (2).

(1) Baseline drift during staged enablement is real. Suggestion:
- Baseline should be computed from “telemetry_v2_enabled=true” traffic only, and only after a segment has at least 24h of data. Until then, alert state = “insufficient baseline”.
- For the first day, we can run “comparison vs last 2h median” as a dashboard-only view, but I would avoid paging until the 24h baseline is established.

(2) saved_prefill_ms: with PR-18436 + PR-18452, we now classify partial-prefill explicitly. We can compute saved_prefill_ms for partials, but it’s noisier. Recommendation: for the pager condition, use saved_prefill_ms aggregated over outcomes=hit only (exclude partial) so the coupling is stable.

(3) Top-N enforcement: we can enforce in the telemetry aggregation (PR-18475) by rolling up to a fixed segment set (region x deployment_mode) and not allowing route/model breakdown in the pager query. If we later want route-level paging, we should do that as a separate phase after we’ve validated cardinality budgets.

I’ll update Sergio offline with suggested language for the proposal.

Logan

---

From: Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 9:16 AM
Subject: Re: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

Great feedback — updated plan below (incorporating Logan + Rafael).

Changes from v3:

A) Baseline gating
- Alerts only evaluate segments where telemetry_v2_enabled=true AND baseline_age >= 24h
- Until then: dashboard annotation “Baseline still warming” + no alert notifications

B) Pager coupling metric
- Pager condition uses saved_prefill_ms on outcomes=hit only (excludes partial)
- We’ll keep a warning-only panel for partial rate spikes (to catch misclassification)

C) Segmentation & Top-N
- Pager evaluates only (deployment_mode, region). No route/model breakdown in pager.
- Warning evaluates same segments; route/model breakdown is dashboard drilldown only.

D) Oncall impact / rollout policy
- Phase 0: deploy templates disabled (no notifications)
- Phase 1: enable warning (non-paging) in us-east-1 Hosted only (48h)
- Phase 2: enable pager in us-east-1 Hosted only (next 48h)
- Phase 3: enable warning in other Hosted regions
- Phase 4: Dedicated warning then pager (after Hosted stable)

E) Rollback
- Connor will have a one-click playbook:
  - disable alert notifications (global)
  - disable v2 cache telemetry flag (per region/tier)
- Runbook link will be embedded in alert description.

F) New guardrail alert (non-paging)
- “Cache telemetry cardinality guardrail triggered” routed to #eng-sre-alerts

Allison: can you do a quick pass for standards compliance (naming, runbook, owner tags)?

Sean/Rafael: if the above matches what you want, can I get explicit “approved to proceed” so we can merge PR-921 changes and schedule rollout with Connor?

Sergio

From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

Reviewed. With the updates, it aligns with our observability standards.

Notes / nits:
- Please set alert owner to “eng-sre-observability” and include the oncall rotation name explicitly in the pager.
- In the alert description, specify that the segmentation is (deployment_mode, region) by design and route/model is dashboard-only.
- For the guardrail alert, include the cardinality budget doc link (ADR-027) in addition to the data quality runbook.

Otherwise +1.

Allison

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Costa <sergio.costa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 24, 2025 at 12:05 PM
Subject: Re: Cache hit-rate regression alerts rollout (SRE approval)

Approved to proceed with the updated plan.

Conditions for sign-off (capturing what we discussed):
- No paging until baseline_age >= 24h AND warnings have run in us-east-1 Hosted for 48h without high noise.
- Pager scope stays at (deployment_mode, region) for this rollout.
- Rollback playbook must be validated by Connor (dry-run in staging) before Phase 1.

Rafael — please keep an eye on oncall noise during Phase 1/2 and flag immediately if the warning channel is too chatty.

Sergio — once you’ve incorporated Allison’s nits, please drop a note in #eng-sre with rollout dates.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
